- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for 30-day horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged flat or downward trend — reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for next 7–14 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to lag — add 1–2% upward bias to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 prior days, apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.00/0.20/0.40), model often fails to capture sentiment shifts — use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day prices to anchor forecast.
